text.text_excerpt: If you're looking for something fun to do but low key - I'd recommend this. We came right before Tropical Storm Gordon, and much of the city was closing up shop till the storm passes, so we were glad to see this spot open. It's cheap and will kill an hour or so. It was quite dark and stormy that day, so it added to the spookiness of it all. Jagger was a pretty good tour guide, though maybe not the most knowledgeable about Zack and Addie - Which is easily the highlight of the tour. Good thing I didn't know a thing about it before we went. It was a really cool, creepy surprise. I don't wanna give too much away, but I thought this was a fun little stop. Don't let the kitsch name throw you off. This place is really interesting and absolutely FOR YOU if you want an interesting and informative slice of haunted NOLA. I did the cemetery tour & toured the house & booked a reading with Sharon Graham. The cemetery tour was led by locally born & raised Gina who gives you the real NOLA and cuts away the years of debris floating around rumors about NOLA that just aren't true, many of which I believed. Gina does an informative & fun tour. Now. If you've always wanted a psychic tarot reading or you've had 100 and are tired of how inaccurate or "reaching" they can be, book with Sharon Graham. We were really excited to visit the museum because we have taken a Bloody Mary tour and she was awesome! We walked in and saw Bloody Mary right away and asked for the museum tour. She said she would be leading it which we stoked to get her! She also gave us a discount because we were returning clients, which was super sweet of her! The museum is creepy and beautiful, with so many different items to look at. The best part for us was the upstairs. I have been long captivated by the story of Zack and Addie, and to be able to see where the murder happened was nothing short of haunting.
